consumer_complaint_narrative:
To Whom It May Concern, I would like to submit a complaint about Discover Credit Card services. They have repeatedly made it sound as if there were options other than what I was already working with when those options were not available. This issue started when I missed a payment earlier this month due to my hours having been reduced and not having the ability to make the payment before the due date. I had been planning on paying the overdue amount as soon as I was able to later in the month.

Shortly after the missed payment, I started receiving calls from Discover a minimum of 3 times each day. When I listened to the voicemail, the message had stated that there were money saving options if I reached out to them to discuss it. I reached out through chat on XX/XX/XXXX  and spoke with XXXX. 

During my conversation with XXXX I had explained my situation and she ignored my original request for information about the options mentioned in the voicemail. She repeatedly pressured me to set up a payment plan without actually answering my question. I had to ask more than once for an explanation of the options. Once she finally addressed the question I was told I was already on a plan and there were no options. The only option offered at this point was to pay the past due now and the rest by the next payment date. When asking about why there were no other options and was informed that once a program is accepted there are not any other options. 

At this point I was also told that my payments would go back to {$190.00} after the current amount was paid in full. This was higher than my prior payments and when I questioned it and asked if there was a supervisor to review the account, I was told that the payment fluctuates with the balance and she was an account manager and there was no one else to review the account. 

I then brought up Discovers late payment forgiveness program since I dont believe I had missed a payment prior to this and was told they would forgive the fee if I set up a payment with them now. This was after I had already explained that I could not make a payment at this time. 

Finally I planned to submit a complaint since they would not allow me to talk to a supervisor and I felt the voicemail that was left was misleading. Once I mentioned this to XXXX she finally transferred me to a supervisor. I then spoke with XXXX who offered to remove the interest fees and late fee for the previous month. This was only allowed if I were to set up a payment at this time. This would have assisted a small amount but would not have changed the amount the payment I was having trouble with would be. I asked about any types of options to make future payments more affordable and was told again that there were no other options. He also suggested splitting the payment due up over multiple months but I would incur late fees each month if the account was not brought fully up to date. 

At this point he also pointed out that I could pay extra on each payment to make the principal reduce faster. This felt like a foolish statement as I was already having trouble making the minimum payment. They continued to try to get a payment set up and I had looked away for a minute to check something to see what I could do when the chat was ended abruptly. 

My Second conversation with Discover was on XX/XX/XXXX  when I tried to confirm that my account was eligible for the late payment forgiveness when I would be able to make the payment. I reached XXXX who transferred me to XXXX since my account was on a payment plan. XXXX then proceeded to tell me that in order to see if I qualified for a different payment plan they could drop my current plan and check. They also continued to pressure me to set up a payment when I had said I could not make one at the time.

The same credit was offered and I was told it would not lower the minimum payment due. I agreed to trying to change programs and see if a better option was available. There were no other options and I was not able to be put back on my current plan. 

When I reached back out on XX/XX/XXXX  after receiving another voicemail stating there were options, I was informed by XXXX that you are not able to be put on a new program within a year of having been on one. This means that the prior associate I spoke with falsely offered me a chance to change my program when that was not an option. If the prior associate XXXX had not offered this, I would not have ended my payment plan and would have done my best to get a payment in before the upcoming due date. 

This complaint is being submitted due to the deceptive practices used by Discover in trying to get me to contact them as well as the blatant lie about what options there might potentially be if I ended the program I was on at the time. Attached as supporting documentation is a copy of the transcript from all 3 chat conversations as well as images of the chat screens. 

Sincerely, XXXX XXXX

The first section provides for the option to purchase the vehicle from them, or a party they designate, for the following : ( i ) Residual Value ( explicitly stated as {$10000.00} ) plus ( ii ) a Purchase Option Fee of {$990.00} plus ( iii ) any official fees ( e.g., taxes, tags, license, and registration ). The second section acknowledges that if I reside in a state ( such as FL where I live ) where a seller needs a motor vehicle dealer license that I must process this through the Lessor ( Dealer ) or another authorized, licensed dealer selected by Hyundai. The only other language is that I must notify them 30 days prior to exercising for them to make appropriate arrangements, if necessary. 

I have contacted them 30 days prior as well as multiple times since. They continue to direct me to dealerships ( which I would imagine are related parties via a franchise agreement and they likely have contractual rights to ensure the dealerships abide by these contracts ). The issue is that the dealerships will not permit me to exercise my contractual right and purchase the vehicle with the items and amounts set forth in the contract. Rather, every dealership I have spoken with ( XXXX ) quotes me {$1500.00} - {$3000.00} in additional fees above and beyond what is in my contract. I have a proposal from one such dealership as an example in writing as evidence ( as well as the lease ). This proposal includes items such as " Selling Price '' of the vehicle, rather than the Residual Value, above and beyond the Residual Value. It includes other fees such as " Service Fee '' ( not in contract ), taxes/license/tag fee ( which is fine ), but also " E-Tag File '', " Priv-Tag-Agency ''. " Documentation Fee '', " FL Documentation Stamps '', etc.

Due to this, I am unable to exercise my buyout per the contractual agreement I have with Hyundai, which, though I am not a lawyer, by definition should be a breach of contract on their end. There was none of these additional fees in the contract, no mention of being subject to dealership mark-ups, and at the dealership when signing lease, I was informed the amounts in the contract are the only ones I would need to pay to buyout the vehicle. 

Over the past 3 months, I have contacted Hyundai Motor Finance various times requesting assistance or for them to make arrangements to complete this, which they have failed to do. '' Assistance with this would be greatly appreciated and if I am incorrect in my interpretation of this legal issue, I am happy to remove this complaint. 

If I am correct, I imagine there are likely thousands and thousands of consumers in the state of Florida who have simply accepted this practice, had their contracts breached, and had significant amounts of money taken from them, despite having a contractual agreement. Here we are 2 years later and I check my XXXX XXXX to ensure that my credit report is accurate and I see this account on my report. I explained to XXXX that I didn't owe any money to XXXX ; and if I did, why didn't they ever bill me or call me about this debt? XXXX went on to explain that her company had sent me a bill this past XX/XX/XXXX. She said she sent it to a XXXX XXXX address. Unfortunately, I don't live at the XXXX XXXX address. I informed her of that fact and XXXX went on to explain that is why I didn't know about the bill. She said that is also why I didn't receive a bill from XXXX either. I could almost understand her logic but I had to correct her because it was based on a faulty premise. consumer_complaint_narrative:
In the evening of XX/XX/XXXXXXXX XXXX  I was approached by three large men outside XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX in XXXX while loading groceries into my car. They asked for my attention and seemed cordial ; one started talking about how his son was XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX and that they were going around trying to raise money for his funeral. I felt cornered, as I was alone at the time and still loading bags of groceries into my car. They were also blocking my path to the drivers side door of my car. It was dark and cold, and I was in the far corner of the parking lot so there were very few people around. I felt pressured, so I offered to donate {$10.00}. They claimed that due to some legal reasons they were not allowed to accept cash, and so they asked me for my card. They also claimed that they needed to check something sent to my phone and one of them took my phone from me - I had been holding and using my phone at the time, and the man plucked it out of my hands upon asking the question. I did not want to give up my unlocked phone, but I felt unsafe and cornered and did not object as I did not know what they would do to me otherwise. They also handed me a clipboard with a sheet for me to fill in my info during this time, and held my phone away from me so I could not see what they were doing on it. I attempted to look at what they were doing on my phone multiple times but they held it just out of my view. After making the charge, they gave me back my card and phone and left. 

Their behavior with my phone made me suspicious, so as soon as I got in my car, I checked the charges on my card and saw that there was a charge for {$5000.00} to XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, which is a merchant I had never heard of and a charge that was grossly in excess of what I agreed to donate. I later looked online and could not find any evidence of the merchant existing. I also checked my text messages to see if there was a verification or notification XXXX  that had been sent or responded to, but could not find XXXX ; I assume that XXXX was sent that they quickly responded to and deleted. I immediately called the Chase fraud line to get my card locked and I let the associate know what had happened. He said that he would cancel my card, get a new one sent to me, and put a note on my account. He also told me that the charge would be reversed in about 48 hours, which it was. I was shaking and scared for the entire rest of the day, and this was compounded by the fact that I had not thought to write fake personal information down on the clipboard they gave me and for a while I was very scared that they might try to follow me or come to my home upon finding out that Id canceled the card. Ive been too scared to go out into the city alone since then as well. 

On XX/XX/XXXX, I received a notice from Chase letting me know that the fraud department had finished its review and concluded that I was responsible for the transaction because I received benefit from this transaction. The charge was added back onto my account. I disputed the charge, as at no point did I agree to pay the amount that was charged to my card. 
This was a scam that intentionally abused the fact that I was a woman alone in the dark, confronted and cornered by three men - XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX 

As soon as I received the letter from Chase that denied my fraud claim, I called again to try to figure out what further steps I could take as at that point I was very confused. I felt I had done everything right in calling the fraud department minutes after the event transpired and getting my card canceled. They directed me to the disputes department, and when I called that department they informed me that I had to type and send a physical letter to their customer service office to open a dispute, alongside any more information I wished to provide. I promptly did so ; this letter is a slightly modified and updated version of the letter I sent to the Chase customer service department. I received a response from Chase on XX/XX/XXXX in the form of another letter that said they had resolved my dispute. I have attached this letter below, but the gist of it is that they found that I either received the services or the merchant made them available for my use and they cant confirm Im due a credit because the services I purchased were received or available to use. 

By this point I was extremely upset and confused, especially since the amount that they fraudulently charged me for was an amount that was, and still is, lowering my credit score as it accounts for over half of the limit on my credit card. On XX/XX/XXXX I went into a local Chase branch to try to get this situation resolved. I explained what had happened to the representative who met with me, and she was immediately sympathetic after hearing me out and reading my written statement ( the same one I had sent to the customer service office a few weeks prior ). She advised me to get a police report written up about the situation, which I had not thought to do prior as I was extremely shaken after the events initially transpired and thought that reporting things to the fraud department and getting my card canceled would be enough. I went to a local police station that same day and met with an officer, who wrote up a police report on the events and gave me a copy to give to the Chase representative, which I did later that day. 

I received another notice from Chase on XX/XX/XXXX asking for further information on my dispute, which again confused me as Id provided every document and piece of evidence that I had up until that point. I booked another appointment with the Chase representative who I had met with earlier and met with her again on XX/XX/XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXX She did her best to help me dispute the transaction and get the charge lifted from my card, but to no avail. Ultimately, the system that had the final say was not something she had any control over, and despite her best efforts, Chase again determined that the disputed transaction was valid and sent me a letter saying so on XX/XX/XXXX. I contacted the representative who had been helping me again, and she advised me to talk to the major credit bureaus to try and make sure that the lingering charge would not continue to affect my credit score, and to see if I would be able to cancel my card without incurring a severe penalty to my credit score. The last letter from Chase said that they would be forwarding my case and the documents it contained to the credit bureaus, but Ive since received a letter from XXXX saying that the disputed item was verified as accurate. 

This process has frustrating, upsetting, and mentally and emotionally exhausting from beginning to end. It is still an ongoing problem ; the fraudulent charge remains on my account and continues to lower my credit score with every update. Every time I have tried to get this situation resolved, Ive been shut down with short letters devoid of detail that fail to address even the most basic aspects of this case. In addition, the event itself is something I hate being forced to constantly recall as it makes me feel very scared and unsafe whenever I think about it. It especially scares me that, considering their sole intent was to scam others out of money, the men who cornered me almost surely had a weapon. I am very upset about how Ive been treated by Chase throughout this entire process, and I am sick and tired of still having to deal with this event almost six months after it transpired. In addition, the effect that this single transaction has been having on my credit score means I am continuously being punished for XXXX XXXX and my bank refuses to do anything about it. I have attached all relevant documents that I have access to, and I can provide any additional details if needed. I feel that I have exhausted all other options without getting anywhere, which is why I am now filing a complaint through the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau. While I do not wish to pursue legal action on this, I will be contacting an attorney if filing this complaint does not lead to this situation being resolved.

Contradictory Positions & Litigation Abuse PRA represents to the CFPB and credit bureaus that it is investigating disputed accounts and has agreed to cease communications, yet at the same time pursues default judgments in Justice Court, assertingfalselythat I failed to respond. Court records and PRAs own filings show this representation is untrue. PRA filed motions for default judgment while disputes were active, despite the docket reflecting ongoing participation and correspondence PRA while in dispute tells the. 

PRA relies on Justice Court leniency and assembly-line default practices, filing default motions without having first filed admissible business records or ownership proof. When challenged, PRA submits substituted affidavits and custodian declarations on the day of court, depriving me of due process and meaningful opportunity to contest standing or accuracy. 

No Proof of Ownership or Accuracy At no time has PRA produced : A 1099-C A Bill of Sale identifying my specific accounts Account-level purchase schedules Trust-level or securitization exclusion documents Any original creditor agreement establishing lawful transfer of receivables Instead, PRA relies on conclusory affidavits and third-party business records, which are hearsay and insufficient to establish standing, ownership, or accuracy. 

Improper Credit Reporting During Litigation Despite claiming to investigate and cease communications, PRA continues publishing negative tradelines to XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX while actively litigating the same accounts. PRA can not lawfully report disputed debts as accurate while simultaneously claiming investigation and pursuing default. This conduct misrepresents the legal status of the debt and exerts unlawful leverage. 

Statutory Violations PRAs conduct constitutes : Failure to conduct a reasonable investigation and failure to correct inaccurate information in violation of FCRA 1681s-2 ( b ) False and misleading representations regarding default, ownership, and legal status in violation of FDCPA 1692e Unfair and unconscionable collection practices, including litigation during active disputes, in violation of FDCPA 1692f Failure to properly investigate and correct disputed information under Texas Finance Code 392.202 Regulatory Concern PRA tells regulators and credit bureaus one story ( we are investigating ; we ceased communication ) while telling courts another ( the consumer did not respond ; default is proper ). These positions can not simultaneously be true. This pattern reflects willful noncompliance, not isolated error. 

Requested CFPB Action I respectfully request : CFPB supervisory escalation and enforcement review An order requiring PRA to cease all credit reporting on disputed accounts while litigation and investigations are pending Mandatory production of full account-level proof of ownership and accuracy, or Immediate deletion of all PRA tradelines and cessation of litigation activity PRA should not be permitted to weaponize the courts while publishing disputed information to consumer reporting agencies without proof. 

Bottom Line This is not a documentation disputeit is a pattern of coordinated litigation and credit-reporting abuse designed to force payment without proof. CFPB intervention is necessary.

Color of Law and Deprivation of Rights The actions of your organization and its agents have been carried out under the color of law, which is the appearance or use of lawful power to mask an illegal act. If we do not receive a response from the furnisher or the vendor within the required period, we update the item as you have requested or delete the information and send you the results. 

In some instances, we are able to determine whether the disputed information should be changed or deleted without having to contact the furnisher or the vendor. Missing a payment by a few days won't affect your credit scores, but it could have other consequences, such as late fees and rescinded benefits.

Late payments get reported to the credit bureaus when your creditor sends an update to the bureaus and your payment is at least 30 days late. One exception is with federal student loans, which don't get reported as late until you're at least 90 days past due.

Creditors send updates to the credit bureaus at different times, and there's no way to know exactly when the late payment status will show up. But many creditors send updates monthly, so you could expect the late payment to appear on your credit report within a month or two of falling behind on your payments.

Creditors use different codes to indicate your account 's status. There's a code for when your account is current and a code for when your account is 30 days past due. There are also codes for when you fall further behind : 60, 90, 120, 150 or 180 or more days past due.

But there's no code for an account being one to 29 days late, so your creditors may report your account is current if your payment is only a few days late. '' The very last paragraph validates my point to Experian representative about XXXX reporting my XXXX loan 30 days past due. Although there were circumstances outside of my control for why the payment was late, XXXX confirmed that it received payment for my account on XX/XX/year>. From XX/XX/year> to XX/XX/year> is XXXX calendar days. If my account was 19 days past due on XX/XX/year>, that means it was 29 days past due on XX/XX/year> which is still not 30 days past due. However, XXXX is reporting that I was 30 days past due despite it's own correspondence to me that the timeline was not accurate. 

This communication was forwarded to Experian through the CFPB complaint about the inaccurate information reporting on my consumer report. Although Experian sent disclosure stating that it could intervene and modify or delete inaccurate information and although Experian 's website states that an account can only be reported as 30 days past due if it is 30 days or more unpaid after the statement date, Experian refuses to modify the information.

consumer_complaint_narrative:
I'd like to make a complaint about Chase 's deceptive use of flexible financing offers ( " My Chase Plan '' ) and its use of the term " interest saving balance ''.

I am someone who pays off my credit card, in full, every month. I have all of my cards set up on autopay so that they pay the full balance each month without any intervention from me. 

In XXXX, I made a large purchase of {$10000.00} on my card for a medical expense - a charge that I would normally have paid off in full that month - and Chase contacted me with a promotional offer to set up a flexible financing plan, or " My Chase Plan '' to spread that charge over 9 months, with 0 interest and 0 fees. While I have never in my life carried a balance on any credit card before, the promotional offer enticed me, since it was completely free. When I set up the plan, I was required to change my autopay settings from paying the " Statement Balance '' to paying an " Interest Saving Balance ''. Chase describes the difference between those two options as follows on the autopay page : " [ 'Statement Balance ' ] would pay off the total amount of your flexible financing offers at once. If you'd like to pay the monthly amount instead for the flexible financing offers you set up and avoid interest on new purchases, please choose " interest saving balance. '' For a few months, Chase auto-paid itself varying amounts each month, from {$1100.00} to {$1100.00}. I continued to make small purchases on my card, which I assumed were being paid off through this " Interest Savings Balance. '' Although the numbers were impossible for me to interpret due to the carried balance subject to my flexible financing offer, the amount charged varied each month and the total balance seemed to go down over time. Moreover, each month 's statement contained a section reading as follows, and leading me to believe that the total amount of new purchases each month were being included in each monthly autopayment : " What is an Interest Saving Balance? Pay the Interest Saving Balance every month by your due date to avoid interest on new purchases and avoid prematurely paying off your flexible financing offer balances. This amount includes your current statement new balance, minus your total balance for flexible financing offers, plus your monthly payment due for all flexible financing offers. It doesnt include disputed amounts. '' Suddenly, in XXXX, I received a standard email notification of an upcoming autopayment, which indicated that my " Interest Saving Balance '' that month was over {$5600.00}. I quickly logged on to check my card, as I did not remember making a large charge that month and was concerned that I could be the victim of fraud. But I only saw my usual, small purchases. I also checked all of my account settings to ensure nothing had changed and that I was still set up to pay the " Interest Saving Balance ''. Unable to figure out what was going on after studying my account and past statements for over 30 minutes, I called Chase. A representative was also perplexed, and took 15 minutes to study my account. Finally, she came back and explained that, contrary to what Chase had represented to me at the time I signed up for the flexible financing offer, contrary to what is shown on its autopay settings page on its website, and contrary to what is in every monthly statement I have received since XXXX, Chase was NOT including my new monthly charges in the autopay amount of " Interest Saving Balance '' each month. She explained that, unbeknownst to me, there was a promotional 0 % APR rate on my card until XX/XX/XXXX, so all of the charges I made from XXXX to XXXX had not been auto-paid, and were instead accumulating every month, only to suddenly come due in XXXX. None of this was properly disclosed. I frankly had no idea that there was any temporary promotional 0 % APR on my card ( since I never carry a balance ), and had no idea that selecting " Interest Saving Balance '', as I was required to do, would cause me to accumulate additional debt that was not being paid off every month. In fact, each month 's statement directly represents the opposite, saying that the " Interest Saving Balance '' " includes your current statement new balance, '' and further saying that " any promotional purchase APR offers '' are not included in the " flexible financing offers '' that are deducted from that Interest Saving Balance each month.

In this instance, I have not been financially harmed by Chase 's misrepresentations, other than perhaps through a small hit to my credit score. I was not charged any late fees or interest, and although I am surprised by the sudden {$5600.00} charge, I am fortunate to be able to pay it in full without issue. That being said, this practice was clearly misrepresented to me, and presumably other consumers, and Chase 's misrepresentations constitute, in my view, abusive and predatory lending practices that could seriously harm those who are less financially advantaged. I hope that the CFPB will investigate this and ensure that Chase updates its practices and disclosures so that other consumers are not harmed by sudden undisclosed charges.

We attempted to get a loan modification from Chase but, unbeknownst to us, were put into a situation which later came to be known as " dual tracking. Unfortunately, none of the benefits of the new legislation nor any of the money from the big fines paid did anything to help my situation. 

The " dual tracking '' worked like this : On the side visible to us, we had a " single point of contact '' who took our loan mod application, discussed with us our options and told us what we had to do to get the loan modification. My non-payment during that underwriting period not only reflected the agreement between myself and the loan modification department, I was told that there would be a penalty for making a payment, i.e. total reset of the agreed upon loan modification.

consumer_complaint_narrative:
I had been getting mailers from Bankers Healthcare Group ( BHG ) for over a year saying that I was prequalified for up to {$250000.00}. When I decided to open a business in XX/XX/XXXX I had enough working capital. However, there were a lot of unforeseen circumstances That required me to need additional funding. I contacted bankers healthcare group about getting funding. I submitted an application and was contacted by the lending department. I explained the situation and that I was already financially too far in do not get funding. My application was ran by someone in Florida, and I was told that there was an approval and someone would be getting back to me. A day or two later someone from New York called me to tell me that based on my annual income of {$50000.00}, with minimal debt, I had been approved for {$20000.00}. I explained that I really needed to get funding and that at that point I was financially in over my head. I was told that if I had somebody go on the loan with me that I would probably qualify for more. I added my fianc to the loan and a day later I received another communication asking me if there was anybody else that could go on the loan with me. I asked my son-in-law to go on the loan to which he agreed. 
It was stated to me that the loan would not show on any of our credit reports and that there were easy terms and that there were some fees that would be rolled into the loan, but would be refunded at the end of the term. At no time was I ever told that these fees were optional. I was told that they would have to be added in order for the loan to move forward. I was told that I would not be able to make any extra payments towards the loan for the first five years. I disagreed with that and it was changed to one year. 
I was told that in order for the loan to be approved I would need to agree to the monthly payment to be auto drafted from my bank account. I agreed to it. The loan was approved for {$150000.00}. Within a couple of days {$140000.00} was deposited into my account however, my beginning balance was {$160000.00} at an interest rate of 17 %. 
The monthly payment has been {$2900.00}. After a few months I contacted the BHG to inquire how I could obtain a login so that I could closely monitor my loan and I was informed that they do not have any way to track the loan, with the exception of an amortization paper which was sent to me. Likewise, I have not been able to get information on how or where to make extra payments to after the one year. 
In XX/XX/XXXX I contacted BHG to inquire about getting a lowered interest rate or smaller payment amount due to my business financially, struggling and fearing that I would have to close due to not being able to make the monthly bills largely in part due to this payment. I was sent an email with the paperwork needed to fill out, which was very extensive and required more information than when I had originally applied for the loan. They were asking for financial information for myself, my fianc, and my son-in-law. Fearing that we would not be eligible for the hardship, I felt defeated. The paperwork was also asking for information that I was not sure how to provide. 
At the time of this complaint, 15 payments of {$2900.00} have been drafted from my business checking account, leaving a current balanced owed of {$150000.00}. After extensive research I have learned that BHG has had multiple complaints against them for predatory lending practices. 
BGH pushes to get the loan approved without running credit or allowing the borrower the ability to build credit from this loan, the only payment option is for auto withdraw, they require credit insurance without advising that this is option, and high interest rate. 
I am asking that BHG reverse the added fees in the amount of {$17000.00}, lower the interest rate, adjust payments already made to reflect the lower interest and apply the amount to the principal balance, lower the monthly payment to a position that does not create a financial hardship.
